stem: Why should a bleeding history ask specifically about procedures such as tongue-tie release or circumcision?

options.text: They are the most common causes of immune thrombocytopenia
Families may not remember or describe them as surgeries
They commonly cause vitamin C deficiency
They are the only way to diagnose factor XIII deficiency

explanation: Families may not remember or describe them as surgeries. These minor neonatal procedures can be overlooked unless asked about specifically in a bleeding history.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because immune thrombocytopenia is unrelated to whether a child has had minor procedures.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because families may not remember or describe minor neonatal procedures as surgeries, so asking specifically can uncover a relevant bleeding history.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because these procedures do not cause vitamin C deficiency.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because factor XIII deficiency is not diagnosed only by asking about these procedures.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because these procedures do not usually indicate inherited haemophilia.

source.hint: Consider how families might perceive minor neonatal procedures compared to major operations.
